title: Introducing AI Modeler
summary: Meet AI Modeler: build, explain, edit and review financial models in plain language, on live data in Abacum. No formula syntax, no modeling bottleneck.
body_markdown:
**Quick answer:** AI Modeler is an AI agent built into Abacum that builds, explains, edits and reviews financial and operational models from plain language, on your connected data, inside your existing permissions. Every calculation still runs through Abacum's calculation Engine, not a separate AI arithmetic path, and nothing saves until you approve it.


Every planning vendor sells the same promise: connect your data, retire the spreadsheets, close faster. Most of them deliver on the data part. Then they hand you a formula language and a blank canvas, and the promise quietly becomes a project.


This is the part of the category nobody puts on a pricing page. The software is not the cost. The modeling is. Ask any finance team what stood between signing a planning tool and trusting its first forecast, and the answer is rarely the integrations. It is the time spent translating how the business actually works into someone else's formula language, and then going back to whoever did that translation every time something changes.


Finance teams feel this as three separate problems that are really one problem.


-


**The expertise concentrates in one or two people.** In most finance teams, one or two people know the formula language well enough to build with confidence. Everyone else queues behind them, and good ideas wait for calendar space that never appears.


-


**When those people move on, modeling stops.** The models keep calculating. Nobody can change them. New joiners inherit logic they did not write and will not risk touching, so the team works around the model instead of with it.


-


**Models nobody fully understands stop improving.** An FP&A manager who cannot predict what adding a dimension will do to existing logic will not add the dimension. The model stays smaller and simpler than the business it is supposed to describe.


The conclusion is uncomfortable for the whole category: a planning platform is only as useful as the number of people who can change it. In most finance teams, that number is one.


## **Why a chatbot does not solve this**


The obvious answer in 2026 is to point an AI at it, and plenty of teams have tried. Ask a general-purpose assistant to build you a headcount model and you get something that looks right in a chat window and lives nowhere. It is disconnected from your actuals. It does not recalculate. It cannot be a version anyone plans against.


The gap is not language understanding. Modern models handle finance vocabulary fine. The gap is that a model is only worth building if it sits on live data, recalculates against a real engine, and survives being edited six months later by someone who did not build it.


That requires the AI to work inside the planning platform, not beside it.


## **Introducing AI Modeler**


AI Modeler is an AI agent built into Abacum that builds, explains, edits and reviews financial and operational models from plain language. It works on your connected data, inside your existing permissions, and it writes nothing until you approve the plan.


Four things it does, from launch day:


-


**Build.** Describe the model you need. The agent scans your connected datasets, proposes the variables and formulas, and creates a working, saved, editable model once you approve it. "Build me a P&L from my GL data" returns a live model in minutes, not a template you then have to populate.


-


**Explain.** Point it at any model, including one you inherited, and ask how a number gets calculated. It walks the logic step by step, so a handover that used to mean reverse-engineering someone else's formulas now takes a conversation.


-


**Edit.** "Add a marketing spend variable to my OPEX model and break it down by channel." The agent adds the variable, sets up the dimension, updates the totals, and saves on your approval. You no longer need the person who wrote the original formula.


-


**Review.** Ask the agent to look over a model's structure and it tells you where the logic can be simplified and where the build can be made more efficient, in plain language, without you reading a single formula.


## **The part that matters most: the AI never does the math**


Finance teams are right to be skeptical of AI near the numbers, and the architecture is the answer, not a reassurance.


AI Modeler proposes structure and formulas. Abacum's calculation Engine performs every calculation, exactly as it does for a model you build by hand. There is no separate AI arithmetic path and no black box between your inputs and your outputs. If you audit a number the agent built, you audit the same Engine you already trust.


Three more controls sit on top of that:


-


You approve before anything saves. The agent shows you the plan, the variables and the formulas it intends to write. Nothing reaches your model until you say yes.


-


Deletes need explicit confirmation, with the downstream impact shown first.


-


The agent works inside your permissions. It cannot read or change anything you could not read or change manually. Role-based access carries straight through, so rolling it out does not mean loosening anything.


## **What it changes, by role**


-


**FP&A analysts and managers:** the agent is a skill multiplier. Modeling stops being a specialism one person guards and becomes something the whole team does. The person who used to be the bottleneck gets their week back.


-


**Heads of FP&A and VP Finance:** key-person risk on the modeling expert drops sharply. New hires contribute in their first weeks instead of their first quarter. When the business asks for a new model on Tuesday, the answer is Wednesday.


-


**CFOs:** it collapses time to value. Teams reach a working, trusted model faster, and planning keeps moving when people change roles.


-


**Teams outside finance, in RevOps, BizOps and People:** the syntax barrier was the reason they never touched the planning tool. Plain language removes it, and planning becomes something the business does with finance rather than to finance.


## **Start from good practice, not a blank canvas**


AI Modeler also draws on a curated library of model blueprints, extended continuously. Ask it to start you from a blueprint and the model you get already follows proven structural practice, so your first build is closer to your fifth.


Good modeling practice becomes the default instead of the reward for experience.


## **The honest version of the AI promise**


Most AI announcements in finance software promise that the software will do your thinking. We are promising something narrower and more useful: the software will stop making you learn its language before you can do your own thinking.


Describe the model. Get it working on your data. Change it yourself afterwards. No syntax to learn, no consultant to call, and no single person your entire planning process depends on.
